proposal: PR #812: To keep payment calls safe, wrap the call to the card processor in a single global tokio::sync::Mutex. The handler acquires the lock, awaits the processor HTTP call (30 s timeout), then releases. This guarantees we never double-submit.
rationale: Global lock held across a 30 s network await serializes all payments; throughput collapses to one in-flight call and it does not prevent duplicate submissions across replicas.

proposal: Ledger service design: account balances are stored as Java double and summed with +=. Interest is computed as balance * 0.035 / 12 and written back. Fully unit tested.
rationale: Binary floating point for currency causes rounding drift; use integer minor units or BigDecimal.

proposal: Signup flow: SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE username = $1; if no row, INSERT the new user. No unique index needed since we check first.
rationale: Check-then-act race; concurrent signups both pass the check and create duplicates without a unique constraint.

proposal: API quota counter: each of our 12 replicas does GET quota:{user} from Redis, adds 1 in application code, then SET quota:{user}. If the value exceeds 1000 we return 429.
rationale: Non-atomic read-modify-write across replicas loses increments; use INCR or a Lua script.

proposal: Order service: after committing the order row to Postgres we publish OrderCreated to Kafka in the same request handler. If the publish fails we log it; this is rare in practice.
rationale: Dual write without transactional outbox; a crash or publish failure leaves DB and event stream permanently inconsistent.

proposal: Migration plan for removing users.legacy_email: step 1 run ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email; step 2 deploy the app version that no longer reads it.
rationale: Wrong order: the running app still selects the column and errors between steps; requires expand/contract (deploy code first, drop later).

proposal: Password storage: md5(salt + password) with a 16-byte random per-user salt. Salting makes MD5 secure enough for our scale.
rationale: MD5 is fast and GPU-crackable even when salted; use Argon2id/bcrypt/scrypt.

proposal: Session tokens are generated with Math.random().toString(36).slice(2) concatenated twice, giving about 20 random characters, then stored in a cookie.
rationale: Math.random is not a CSPRNG; tokens are predictable. Use crypto.randomBytes / crypto.getRandomValues.

proposal: Add DELETE /api/users/:id to the admin router. It's internal so no auth middleware is attached; the router is mounted on the same public ingress as the rest of the API.
rationale: Unauthenticated destructive endpoint reachable from the public ingress.

proposal: Resilience: on any 5xx from the inventory service, the client retries immediately in a while(true) loop until it succeeds.
rationale: Unbounded retries with no backoff or jitter amplify outages into a retry storm.

proposal: Checkout: if the call to POST /charges times out we automatically retry it up to 3 times. The processor API supports idempotency keys but we don't send one to keep the integration simple.
rationale: Retrying a non-idempotent charge after timeout can double-charge customers.

proposal: Per-user limit of 100 req/min enforced by an in-memory token bucket inside each pod. We run 12 pods behind a round-robin load balancer, so the limit is enforced globally.
rationale: Per-pod buckets allow up to ~1200 req/min per user; not a global limit.

proposal: Staging was failing with a self-signed cert error, so we set verify=False in the requests session and rejectUnauthorized: false in the Node client. We'll ship the same config to production for consistency.
rationale: Disabling TLS verification in production enables MITM.

proposal: Ingestion buffer: events are pushed onto an unbounded in-memory queue (a Python list) and a background thread drains it. Memory is cheap so no cap is needed.
rationale: No backpressure; consumer lag leads to OOM and data loss on crash.

proposal: For easier debugging, the API gateway will log the full JSON body of every request, including /login and /payments, to our shared ELK cluster.
rationale: Logs plaintext passwords and card data; violates PCI DSS and basic secret hygiene.

proposal: The new platform is infinitely scalable with zero downtime and blazing-fast responses. It runs on a single Postgres instance; backups are not needed because the cloud provider is reliable.
rationale: Unquantified, physically impossible claims; single point of failure with no backups.

proposal: To cut auth latency, the JWT middleware decodes tokens with jwt.decode(token, options={'verify_signature': False}) and trusts the role claim.
rationale: Skipping signature verification lets anyone forge admin tokens.

proposal: Outbound calls to partner APIs use the default HTTP client with no connect or read timeout configured; partners have good SLAs.
rationale: No timeouts means a hung partner exhausts worker threads and cascades failure.

proposal: Checkout shows the user's available balance from a Redis cache with a 24-hour TTL. Writes to the balance do not invalidate the cache; the purchase is approved if cached balance >= price.
rationale: Stale authorization data allows overspending; cache must be invalidated or bypassed for the decision.

proposal: The borrow checker rejects our cache update, so we'll use unsafe { &mut *(shared_ref as *const T as *mut T) } to get a mutable reference from a shared one. It's only used in one place.
rationale: Mutating through a pointer derived from a shared reference without UnsafeCell is undefined behavior.

proposal: We will stay a modular monolith for now: 6 engineers, one deployable, module boundaries enforced by ArchUnit tests, p95 latency target 200 ms at 300 RPS. We revisit service extraction if the team exceeds 25 engineers or a module needs independent scaling.
rationale: Monolith is appropriate for team size; has measurable targets and explicit revisit criteria.

proposal: Desktop app local store: SQLite in WAL mode, a single writer thread, busy_timeout=5000, foreign_keys=ON, and an online .backup snapshot nightly. Expected data size under 2 GB, one user.
rationale: SQLite is the right tool for a single-user embedded store; concurrency model is respected.

proposal: API quota: a Redis Lua script does INCR quota:{user}:{minute} and sets EXPIRE 60 on first increment, returning the count atomically. All 12 replicas share the same Redis; >1000 returns 429.
rationale: Atomic shared counter with expiry; correct global limit.

proposal: Pagination for the 50M-row events table uses keyset pagination on (created_at, id) with a composite index; clients pass the last seen pair as an opaque cursor. Page size is capped at 500.
rationale: Keyset pagination is O(log n) per page and stable under inserts.

proposal: Order service writes the order row and an outbox row in the same Postgres transaction. A relay (Debezium) publishes outbox rows to Kafka with at-least-once delivery; consumers dedupe on event_id.
rationale: Transactional outbox plus idempotent consumers gives consistency.

proposal: Removing users.legacy_email via expand/contract: release N stops reading and writing the column; after N is fully rolled out and verified for 7 days, release N+1 runs ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN.
rationale: Correct zero-downtime ordering.

proposal: Passwords are hashed with Argon2id (m=64 MiB, t=3, p=1) per OWASP guidance, with parameters stored alongside the hash so we can rehash on login when we raise cost.
rationale: Memory-hard KDF with upgrade path.

proposal: Session tokens: 32 bytes from crypto.randomBytes, base64url-encoded, stored server-side as SHA-256 hashes, set in HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax cookies with 14-day absolute expiry.
rationale: CSPRNG tokens, hashed at rest, hardened cookie flags.

proposal: Add DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{id}. Requires an authenticated user, verifies the session belongs to the caller (else 404), checks the CSRF token, writes an audit log entry, and returns 204 idempotently if already deleted.
rationale: Destructive route with authN, authZ, CSRF, auditing and idempotency.

proposal: Inventory client retries only idempotent GETs and PUTs on 502/503/504, with exponential backoff and full jitter (base 100 ms, cap 5 s), max 5 attempts, honoring Retry-After, behind a circuit breaker.
rationale: Bounded, jittered retries restricted to idempotent operations.

proposal: Checkout sends an Idempotency-Key (UUIDv4 generated per checkout attempt) on POST /charges and stores it with a unique constraint for 24 h; retries after timeout reuse the same key.
rationale: Idempotency keys make charge retries safe.

proposal: Signup: users.username has a UNIQUE index (case-insensitive via citext). The handler simply INSERTs and maps unique_violation (SQLSTATE 23505) to a 409 'username taken' response.
rationale: Database constraint enforces uniqueness atomically; no race.

proposal: Config hot-reload: a single global RwLock guards the in-memory config struct. A watcher thread parses the new file outside the lock, then takes the write lock only to swap an Arc pointer (microseconds). No I/O happens under the lock; reloads occur at most once per minute.
rationale: Global lock is fine here: tiny critical section, no I/O under lock, rare writes.

proposal: FFI wrapper for libzstd: the unsafe calls are confined to one module, each block has a // SAFETY: comment stating pointer validity and length invariants, the public API is safe, and CI runs Miri on pure-Rust paths plus ASan on the FFI tests.
rationale: Minimal, documented, tested unsafe behind a safe API.

proposal: Build cleanup script: set -euo pipefail; WORKDIR=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf -- "$WORKDIR"' EXIT; with a guard that aborts if WORKDIR is empty or equals /. All artifacts are written under WORKDIR.
rationale: rm -rf scoped to a mktemp directory with guards and strict mode is safe.

proposal: Partner API calls use a 2 s connect timeout and 10 s total deadline, a per-partner bulkhead of 50 concurrent requests, and a circuit breaker that opens after 50% failures over 20 calls.
rationale: Timeouts, bulkheads and breakers contain partner failures.

proposal: Ingestion buffer is a bounded channel (capacity 10,000). When full, the HTTP endpoint returns 429 with Retry-After; poison messages go to a dead-letter queue after 5 attempts. Queue depth is exported as a metric with an alert at 80%.
rationale: Bounded queue with backpressure, DLQ and alerting.

proposal: Ledger stores amounts as BIGINT minor units (cents) with a currency code column; interest calculations use BigDecimal with HALF_EVEN rounding and the result is converted back to minor units once.
rationale: Integer minor units and explicit decimal rounding avoid float error.

proposal: Primary Postgres with one synchronous standby in another AZ and one async replica; WAL archived to object storage for PITR; restore drills monthly. Targets: RPO 0 for AZ loss, RTO under 5 minutes via automated failover.
rationale: Quantified HA/DR targets with tested backups.

proposal: We will not use eval or pickle for the rules engine. Rules are YAML loaded via yaml.safe_load, validated against a JSON Schema, and interpreted by a whitelist of operators; unknown keys are rejected.
rationale: Contains scary keywords only in a negated sense; design is safe.
